claim: On one Windows RTX 4050 host and 100k x 384 AG News rows, all-row completed-call P95 was 16.6567 ms for Qenlo CPU, 3.2404 ms for WGPU predicate, 4.2428 ms for WGPU compact rows, and 4.4591 ms for WGPU mask.
On the same Windows corpus at E=1000 (1% eligible), CPU P95 was 0.2304 ms, compact-row WGPU 0.6766 ms, and shader-predicate WGPU 2.8832 ms; all had recall 1.0.

The post-hoc RTX 4050 compact-row sweep brackets a CPU/WGPU winner reversal between E=2000 and E=3000: CPU/WGPU P95 ratios are 0.8199, 1.1742, 1.2392, 1.2309, 1.1625, and 1.0792 for E=2k,3k,4k,6k,8k,10k.

Applying the shipped 4096-row static rule counterfactually to the six crossover cells misroutes E=3000 and E=4000, with relative P95 regret 17.4239% and 23.9173%; it selects the measured fastest route in the other four cells.

On a separate RTX 4090/Vulkan cohort, one-pass and cached eligibility preparation reduced median run-level P95 versus legacy two-pass at E=1k,4k,6k,100k; all rows retained oracle recall 1.0 at sparse E and 0.99998 at E=100k.

On one Linux RunPod 100k x 384 replay, Qenlo CPU P95 was 12.901 ms, FAISS Flat 10.217 ms, USearch 5.093 ms, FAISS HNSW 1.494 ms, Chroma HNSW 3.777 ms, Milvus Lite 76.229 ms, and LanceDB Flat 242.256 ms; recall ranged 0.9914--1.0.

Author-supplied Android 16/API 36 Mali-G615 results report recall@10=1.0 and no fallback in all 21 cells; at 100k x 384 batch 1 soak, CPU P95 27.019 ms and WGPU exact P95 17.678 ms, while batch-8 WGPU P95 11.131 ms.
On one Intel Arc Vulkan device-lab submission, all 21 cells report recall@10=1.0/no fallback; 100k x 384 soak exact WGPU P95 was 4.444 ms versus CPU 16.486 ms, while IVF-Flat was 2.704 ms.

On an RTX A6000, a research PyTorch/CUDA buffered prototype was slower than FAISS GPU Flat at E=1k and 10k but faster at E=100k and 1M; P95 pairs were (0.097541,0.085716), (0.155722,0.137350), (0.567277,0.788721), and (4.668280,6.347464) ms (prototype, FAISS).

On the strict 1M x 768 TopK cohort with E=10026, FAISS GPU Flat P95 was 0.132222 ms, NumPy CPU 0.197311 ms, and a research CUDA prototype 0.170722 ms; all three qualified at recall@10=1.0, while cuVS recall 0.9 was disqualified.

The retained RunPod 100k x 384 replay measured Qenlo CPU 12.901 ms, Qenlo USearch 5.093 ms, Chroma 3.777 ms, FAISS Flat 10.217 ms, FAISS HNSW 1.494 ms, Milvus Lite 76.229 ms, and LanceDB Flat 242.256 ms P95.

The earlier provider-compatible TopK A6000 experiment reported Qenlo CUDA prototype P95 0.1834 ms versus FAISS GPU Flat 0.1332 ms and cuVS 1.1156 ms at approximately 1% eligibility; all had supplied-ground-truth recall 1.0 in that cell.
The reduced campaign contains 182 retained rows: 131 completed, 42 failed_or_unavailable, 7 failed, and 2 invalid_harness.
On a Runpod RTX 4090 Vulkan host, corrected 100000 x 768 rows have FP64-oracle recall 1.0 for every retained engine in both d4 (batch 1, k=1, unfiltered) and d5 (batch 8, k=64, 10% eligible) cells.
Corrected d4 P95 completed-call latency is Qenlo CPU 9.409 ms, Qenlo WGPU 0.897 ms, FAISS Flat 14.800 ms, NumPy 15.343 ms, Torch CPU 18.695 ms, and Torch CUDA 0.671 ms.
Corrected d5 P95 completed-call latency is Qenlo CPU 28.599 ms, Qenlo WGPU 0.896 ms, FAISS Flat 3.055 ms, NumPy 6.202 ms, Torch CPU 2.936 ms, and Torch CUDA 0.384 ms.

For corrected d5 WGPU, Qenlo-owned accelerator allocation is 314.909 MB, process RSS high-water mark is 1.174577 GB, device scoring is 0.072 ms, selection is 0.613 ms, and backend execution is 0.826 ms; corrected d4 allocation is 311.181 MB and RSS is 1.203675 GB.

On the 10000 x 384 unfiltered RTX 4090 WGPU lifecycle run, add-one, delete-one, add-batch, and delete-batch first-search P95 values are 0.598, 0.631, 0.740, and 0.819 ms respectively; mutation cells rebuilt zero times, deletion checks passed, reopen took 52.169 ms, and the separate first search after reopen took 101.296 ms with one rebuilt resident state.

The lane-minimum selector candidate wins 5 and loses 7 of 12 qualified frozen-baseline pairs; it is rejected as an unconditional replacement, while the durable/local implementation retains the simpler full-rescan selector.
Qenlo WGPU is faster than Chroma in seven qualified paired cells, with observed Chroma/Qenlo P95 ratios from 3.700x to 3233.136x; three Chroma rows fail the predeclared recall gate.
The campaign preserves four pre-fix 100000 x 768 failures, two initial invalid-harness rows, three Chroma recall-gate failures, and 42 unavailable primary-configuration rows.

The final captured Runpod account daily spend is 0.9400778694252952 USD, no campaign pods remain, and the campaign retained no volume. The ledger began at 0.9096019977878312 USD; the observed account-spend delta is 0.030475871637464 USD and is not a definitive campaign-only cost because billing attribution and lag are not isolated.
The only completed but unqualified matrix row is USearch on d2-r25000-d384-b64-k10-f1: recall_at_k=0.3453125 and P95=83.313304 ms; it is excluded from qualified latency comparisons.
Canonical ingestion and query normalization produce FP32 vectors using an FP64 norm accumulator; non-finite, zero-norm, and dimension-invalid inputs are rejected.
The CPU path is exhaustive over eligible canonical rows, but its scoring pipeline contains an FP32 candidate stage and an FP64 final ranking boundary.
Native CPU, native GPU host merge, WGSL selector, and TorchIndex define deterministic distance-then-ID ordering within their implementation precision.
EligibilityPlan binds predicate materialization and representation to the canonical generation and supports one-pass, legacy two-pass, and generation/filter-keyed cached preparation.
Exact row execution validates eligible row ordering, bounds, liveness, and predicate membership; malformed or stale rows fail closed.
Required-GPU mode returns initialization/preparation/search errors rather than silently falling back; automatic mode may use CPU and records a fallback reason.
File-backed commit validates a whole ordered batch before WAL publication and canonical visibility; in-memory mutation has no durability guarantee.
Resident exact GPU state can be updated incrementally after add/delete when capacity, layout, chunk, and budget constraints permit; otherwise a later preparation can rebuild it.

TorchIndex supports the device type names CPU, CUDA, and MPS, with availability checks, but current repository tests provide CPU conformance and negative CUDA coverage rather than positive CUDA/MPS evidence.
TorchIndex.from_collection captures a filtered generation and sequential search rejects the view after a canonical mutation.

The old appendix can describe an FP64 oracle and deterministic ordering, but its wording that tied cutoffs accept only deterministic members selected by that order overstates cross-engine oracle equivalence.
The current phrase 'Atomic batches publish only after validation and durable staging' requires a file-backed qualifier.
A double-checked concurrent TorchIndex snapshot guarantee is not supported by the current source.
